subject: tourism
title: Transport for Tourism
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

They comprise 2.0 percent of the road network
They connect state capitals to the main cities
They carry 40 percent of road-based traffic

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The Yamuna Expressway connects ________ with the world-renowned site Taj Mahal in Agra. (b) The National Waterway running from Sadiya to ________ is 891 km long.
questions.answer: (a) Delhi. (b) Dhubri.

questions.q: Answer in one or two words. (a) Which two cities are joined by the North-South corridor? (b) Which mode of transport has helped in promoting tourism?
questions.answer: (a) Srinagar and Kanyakumari. (b) Air transport (rail and road also help).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The earliest type of boat was the ________. (b) The ________ train has the oldest steam locomotive engine in India.
questions.answer: (a) Raft. (b) Fairy Queen.

questions.q: True or False. (a) Rail transport has transformed the whole world into a global village. (b) Road transport is a flexible and reliable means of transport.
questions.answer: (a) False: air transport has made the world a global village. (b) True.

questions.q: Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Palace on Wheels (b) Heritage on Wheels. B: (i) Bikaner, Gajner, Nawalgarh, Mandawa (ii) Seven-day royal train through Rajasthan, Delhi and Agra (iii) Oldest steam engine.
True or False. (a) National Highways are about 2% of the road network but carry 40% of road traffic. (b) About 97% of international tourists arrive in India by rail.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: about 97% arrive by air.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) India has the ________ largest railway network in the world. (b) The Golden Quadrilateral connects Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and ________.
questions.answer: (a) Fourth. (b) Chennai.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain any two characteristics of the Bharat Darshan special tourist train.
questions.answer: It is an affordable package that covers important tourist places of the country. The fare includes accommodation in the coaches, tourist buses for sightseeing, hall accommodation at night halts and guides.

or.q: Explain two advantages of rail transportation for tourists.
or.answer: It is cheap and comfortable for long distances. A large number of people can travel together and the network reaches nearly all parts of the country.

questions.q: Explain the relationship between transportation and tourism in two points.
questions.answer: Transport links the tourist-generating area with the destination, so tourism is impossible without it. Its capacity, speed, comfort and safety decide the pace of tourist flow.

questions.q: Mention any two measures to boost tourist transport.
questions.answer: Give clear information on location, distance, fares and timetables, and develop standard signs and symbols. Improve infrastructure, keep terminals clean and have a tourist police for help.

questions.q: Write two characteristics of air transport.
questions.answer: It is the fastest mode and saves time over thousands of kilometres. It is free from surface hindrances such as mountains and deserts and offers comfort and luxury.

questions.q: Give two characteristics of road transport.
questions.answer: It is flexible, reliable and cheaper and can take the tourist up to the final destination. Vehicles such as cars, buses, taxis and jeeps connect rail, air and water transport.

questions.q: Name any two tourism-promoting trains and state what each offers.
questions.answer: Palace on Wheels is a luxury seven-day royal train covering Rajasthan, Delhi and Agra. The Fairy Queen has the oldest steam engine and takes tourists to Alwar and Sariska.

questions.q: What is the Golden Triangle? Why is it popular?
questions.answer: It is the route connecting Delhi, Agra and Jaipur, about 1,000 km long. It is popular because tourists visit the Taj Mahal at Agra and Jaipur and the desert areas around it.

questions.q: Mention any two features of water transport for tourism in India.
questions.answer: It includes coastal shipping, inland waterways and sea transport, with cruises on rivers, lakes and backwaters. India has a 7,500 km coastline, 12 major ports and National Waterways such as Allahabad–Haldia.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe any three characteristics of road transportation.
questions.answer: (i) It gives basic accessibility, connecting places and people with flexibility and reliability. (ii) It is cheaper and can take the tourist up to the final destination. (iii) Highways, flyovers and different vehicles (cars, coaches, buses) connect rail, air and water transport.

questions.q: Explain the role of air transport in promoting tourism in India.
questions.answer: (i) It is the fastest mode, so tourists reach any place in the world within 24 hours. (ii) About 97% of international tourists arrive by air and Delhi and Mumbai handle over 70%; charter flights can land at 16 international airports. (iii) Airports are being modernised and airlines offer concessional tickets and packages for budget tourists.

or.q: Explain the role of rail transport in promoting tourism in India.
or.answer: (i) The railways are cheap and comfortable for long distances and carry large numbers of domestic tourists. (ii) Tourist trains such as Palace on Wheels, Fairy Queen, Heritage on Wheels and Bharat Darshan promote tourism. (iii) UNESCO heritage rail lines, the Delhi Metro and Kolkata tram add tourist interest.

questions.q: Analyse the role of railways in tourism development in India.
questions.answer: (i) India has the fourth largest rail network and carries the most passengers per kilometre. (ii) Most domestic tourists depend on it for long journeys. (iii) Special tourist trains and heritage lines attract national and international tourists.

questions.q: Explain the role of a tourist transport system in three points.
questions.answer: (i) It links tourist-generating areas with destinations. (ii) The capacity of the transport system decides the pace of tourist flow. (iii) Comfort, speed, safety, discounts and refreshments act as incentives and good or bad experiences stay in the tourist's mind.

questions.q: Distinguish between air transport and water transport (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Air is the fastest; water is the slowest. (ii) Air is costly; water is the cheapest and carries heavy goods easily. (iii) Air transport covers long distances in hours and is free from surface hindrances; water transport gives cruise and boating experiences on rivers, lakes and the sea.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: How is a road map important for tourists? Explain in six points.
questions.answer: (i) It shows the roads of an area and their condition in different seasons. (ii) It shows national, state and district highways and village roads in different ways. (iii) It shows petrol pumps, lodging and boarding facilities and places of public assistance. (iv) The distance matrix tells the distance between places, helping decide the journey and plan time. (v) It helps domestic tourists who travel by road choose routes. (vi) It helps reach destinations that rail and air do not directly serve.

questions.q: How has air transport played an important role in the development of tourism in India? Explain in six points.
questions.answer: (i) It is the fastest mode and covers long distances in a few hours. (ii) About 97% of international tourists arrive by air. (iii) Delhi and Mumbai are the main entry points for over 70% of them. (iv) Charter flights can land at 16 designated international airports. (v) The government is upgrading airports for passenger comfort. (vi) Public and private airlines offer concessional tickets and special packages for lower-budget tourists.

questions.q: Discuss the different means of tourist transport in India, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Road: national and state highways, expressways and the Golden Quadrilateral and Triangle; flexible and reaches the destination. (ii) Rail: cheap for long distances with tourist trains such as Palace on Wheels and Bharat Darshan. (iii) Heritage railways, the metro and the tram add interest. (iv) Air: the fastest, carrying 97% of international arrivals. (v) Water: 12 major ports, inland waterways, cruises and rafting. (vi) The choice depends on geography, distance, time, comfort, safety and fares.
